evals.name: Routes a backend-only diff to backend auditors only
evals.prompt: I have open changes in server/src/db/schema/runs.ts, server/src/db/migrations/0011_sticky_puma.sql and server/src/platform/config.ts. Nothing under client/. Run a PR self-review and tell me which auditors you are dispatching and why, before you dispatch them.
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight.sh first, then routes to onion-architecture, drizzle-orm-patterns, postgresql-table-design, fastify-best-practices (platform/**), security and project-rules. Dispatches no React, Next, frontend-ui-architecture or react-testing-library auditor because the slice for each is empty.
assertions: Runs assets/preflight.sh before dispatching any subagent
Dispatches onion-architecture for server/src files
Dispatches drizzle-orm-patterns and postgresql-table-design for the schema and migration files
Dispatches security even though no obviously security-related file changed
Dispatches project-rules
Does NOT dispatch react-best-practices, next-best-practices, frontend-ui-architecture or react-testing-library
States that a skill with an empty slice gets no subagent
Dispatches all auditors in a single message so they run in parallel

evals.name: A hard-contract violation blocks the merge path
evals.prompt: I added a new file server/src/modules/billing/service.ts whose first line is `const key = process.env.STRIPE_KEY;`. Run the PR self-review and tell me whether I can open a pull request.
evals.expected_output: Preflight raises exactly one CRITICAL from the secrets-provider check citing the file and line, verdict is request_changes, and the answer is that a non-draft PR is blocked until it is fixed or acknowledged. A draft PR is still allowed.
assertions: Reports a CRITICAL finding for process.env in feature code
Attributes it to the deterministic preflight check, not to an LLM auditor
Sets verdict to request_changes
Cites server/src/modules/billing/service.ts with a line number
Recommends injecting through SecretsProvider
States that gh pr create (non-draft) and gh pr ready are blocked
Does not claim the change can be merged as-is

evals.name: A docs-only diff approves with zero findings
evals.prompt: The only thing I changed on this branch is README.md — three typo fixes. Run the PR self-review.
evals.expected_output: Verdict approve with an empty findings list. No auditor invents architecture, security or test findings for a markdown-only diff.
assertions: Sets verdict to approve
Reports zero findings
Explicitly treats zero findings as a valid and good outcome rather than apologising for finding nothing
Does not raise a tests-dimension warning for a docs-only change
Does not dispatch auditors whose slice is empty
States that the gate will allow the PR to be opened

evals.name: Inherited debt is reported, never blocking
evals.prompt: My branch touches server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/trace.ts. That file's client mirror has been out of sync since before my branch existed. Run the PR self-review and tell me if that blocks me.
evals.expected_output: The mirror drift is reported as WARNING, not CRITICAL, because the two sides already differed at the merge-base. It does not block the PR. A drift introduced by this branch would be CRITICAL.
assertions: Compares the mirror state at the merge-base before assigning severity
Reports the pre-existing drift as WARNING, not CRITICAL
States that it does not block opening the PR
Explains that a drift introduced by this diff would be CRITICAL
Does not silently drop the finding either

evals.name: An acknowledgement dies when its file changes
evals.prompt: I acknowledged the CRITICAL finding preflight-002 in server/src/modules/repos/service.ts yesterday with the reason 'handled by the adapter'. I have since edited that file. Can I open the PR now?
evals.expected_output: No. The acknowledgement recorded the file's hash at ack time; the file has changed, so the ack has expired and the finding blocks again. The fix is to re-run the review and re-evaluate the finding against the new code.
assertions: States that the acknowledgement expired because the file changed
Explains that the ack stores the file hash at ack time
Says the CRITICAL blocks the merge path again
Recommends re-running /pr-self-review rather than re-acknowledging blindly
Does not treat the old acknowledgement as still valid
